clue.text: Killing time

parts.note: reads like idling away the hours, but it means the period of the year when game may lawfully be shot

explanation.surface: Someone loafing about, passing the time with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The period when game animals may legally be pursued and shot is literally a time for killing.

clue.text: Slip out of gear

parts.note: sounds like a car's transmission slipping, but gear here is clothing and slipping out of it means taking it off

explanation.surface: A car's gearbox jumping out of gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is slang for clothes, and slipping out of one's clothes is taking them off.

clue.text: Of course it's a better device

definitions.text: Of course it's a better device

parts.words: Of course it's a better device
parts.note: a better is one who bets, and on a race course the machine that pools their stakes is the totalisator

explanation.surface: A claim that some gadget is obviously an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'superior' but means a person who bets; 'course' is a racecourse. The totalisator, which pools bets at British racecourses, is known by this short name.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator is a betting machine found at racecourses, used by people placing bets.

clue.text: Certainly bound to differ

indicators.note: letters that differ from their original order have been rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone sure to disagree, as is their habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differ' rearranges the seven letters of BOUND TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom expressing certainty, equivalent to an emphatic 'surely'.

clue.text: A bit that's appropriate

definitions.meaning: a simple jointed bit placed in a horse's mouth
as a verb, to take for oneself, informally to pinch

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a simple horse's bit and, informally, the act of grabbing something for oneself.

clue.text: He follows the account, showing pain

indicators.note: the word comes after the account abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for an account
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man looking at his bank account and wincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull persistent pain is a synonym, as in a headache or toothache.

clue.text: Manage to speak about school gymnastics

indicators.note: the speaking word goes round the gym abbreviation

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
PE is physical education, the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: Someone succeeding in giving a talk on school gym classes.
explanation.definitionFit: To run or work a business or machine, which is to manage it.

clue.text: Multi-coloured spice cook laid out

indicators.note: laid out suggests spread about, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A colourful array of spices that a cook has laid out on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of SPICE COOK LAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifting patterns of many colours, like the view in a toy with mirrors and coloured glass.

clue.text: There's no telling where it may lead

definitions.text: There's no telling where it may lead

parts.words: There's no telling where it may lead
parts.note: sounds like uncertainty about an outcome, but 'no telling' means kept quiet: a hidden corridor whose destination is kept secret

explanation.surface: A remark that the outcome of some course of action is unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealed corridor in an old house leads somewhere that nobody tells about.

clue.text: Made a searching examination, by all accounts

definitions.text: Made a searching examination, by all accounts

parts.words: Made a searching examination, by all accounts
parts.note: 'by all accounts' usually means 'reportedly', but here it is the books of a company being examined

explanation.surface: A report that someone carried out a thorough inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant's official examination of a firm's books is a search through all its accounts.

clue.text: Runner allowed to take part in different heat

indicators.note: the word for allowed becomes part of, sitting within, the reshuffled letters
a different version of the word is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A runner being permitted to compete in a different qualifying heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' gives ATHE, and 'take part in' sits the allowing word inside; 'Runner' tempts as a river or plant, but the surface's race heat points to the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A track competitor who runs races is a sportsperson of that kind.

clue.text: Were reformed in jug

indicators.note: something reformed is made over in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People who mended their ways while in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is slang for prison, which the surface leans on; here it is a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-mouthed pitcher for water, as on an old washstand.

clue.text: A well-oiled lock?

parts.note: a lock of hair rather than a door lock, greased up into a tuft over the forehead

explanation.surface: A door lock that has been properly lubricated.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle where a front tuft is greased and brushed up, a lock slicked with oil.

clue.text: Just fine!

definitions.meaning: fine as in pleasant weather, or satisfactory

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both even-handed and pleasantly fine, as weather or a middling standard.

clue.text: Certain to see 007 around university

indicators.note: the spy's name goes around the university letter

parts.note: the code number of the fictional spy James Bond

explanation.surface: Someone sure to spot the famous secret agent near a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure or destined to do something, as in 'certain to win'.

clue.text: See something ugly

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to catch a glimpse of
an unsightly thing, as in 'you look a fright'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to spot something, and informally an ugly spectacle, as in 'what a mess you look'.

clue.text: Little girl's wrong to misrepresent the facts

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diana, so a girl's name in miniature, plus the possessive S
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A small girl's mistake leading her to tell a twisted story.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist or skew facts is to misrepresent them.

clue.text: It's clear I've got set back by depression

indicators.note: the reversed word sits next to the depression word
set back means placed in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the letters of I've without the apostrophe
a dent is a small depression in a surface

explanation.surface: Someone admitting a setback has left them depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain to see, obvious, which is what clear means here.

clue.text: Work for Labour, for example

parts.note: reads as campaigning for the political party, but work is a word that can stand for labour

explanation.surface: Someone volunteering for the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another, as 'work' shares meaning with 'labour'.

clue.text: Like dust that could be stellar or otherwise be lunar

definitions.text: Like dust that could be stellar

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Musing on whether cosmic dust comes from the stars or the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a nebula, a cloud of interstellar dust and gas from which stars may form.

clue.text: Abuses the French in their own words

indicators.note: the French article sits inside the French word for words

parts.note: mots is French for words, the language of the French
les is a French form of 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone insulting the French in their own language.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass or assault someone is a form of abusing them.

clue.text: Region that is not a party to Convention

definitions.text: Region that is not a party to Convention

parts.words: Region that is not a party to Convention
parts.note: looks like a country outside a treaty, but conventions here are social norms, and the region's name gives the word for unconventional artists

explanation.surface: A territory that has not signed an international treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical region of the Czech lands, whose name gave us the word for unconventional artistic lifestyles.

clue.text: Close relative runs into trouble

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the word for trouble

parts.note: bother is trouble or fuss
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A family member who keeps getting into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sibling, one of the closest family relations.

clue.text: Alien girl takes team leader to heart

indicators.note: taking something to heart puts it in the centre of the girl's name

parts.note: Marian is a girl's name

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial woman becoming fond of a sports captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A being from the planet Mars, the classic science-fiction alien.

clue.text: Spheres in sight

definitions.meaning: poetically, the eyes, the organs in which sight lies

explanation.definitionFit: The word means globes, and in poetry the eyes, the round organs of seeing.

clue.text: One's central heating system that runs cold if rattled?

definitions.text: One's central heating system that runs cold if rattled?

parts.words: One's central heating system that runs cold if rattled?
parts.note: a household boiler reading, but it is the body's warm circulating fluid, which runs cold when one is frightened

explanation.surface: A grumble about a temperamental home boiler.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's circulating fluid keeps us warm, and a fright is said to make it run cold.

clue.text: They support British artists

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, members of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Patrons who back homegrown British painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergarments that support the bust, so items that give support.

clue.text: Bull or cow to make an impression

definitions.meaning: the males and females of this marine mammal are called bulls and cows
to stamp wax with a mark

explanation.definitionFit: The marine mammal whose sexes are called bull and cow, and a stamp that presses a mark into wax.

clue.text: Leisure facility

definitions.meaning: facility as in effortlessness, doing something without difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both relaxed rest and the effortlessness of doing something skilfully.

clue.text: The Italian's left with head cold perhaps

parts.note: il is an Italian word for 'the'
a ness is a headland, as in place names like Sheerness

explanation.surface: An Italian man left with a bad cold in his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold is one example of being unwell, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: He has a fish for curing

parts.note: taken as written
the ling is an elongated sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A man who owns a fish for preserving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curing' suggests preserving fish by smoking or salting, but it means making well.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoring someone to health, which is what curing them means.

clue.text: He gives marching orders for more than one material worker

parts.note: drill is a stout twilled cotton cloth
serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth
a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A person giving the sack to workers who handle fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marching orders' usually means dismissal, but here it is commands on a parade ground; the two materials are both fabrics used for uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer who trains recruits by shouting commands on the parade ground.
